purpose: v2 remote run (beads oml-xnn, oml-9kp): the pair verb and the HTTP-only verb set driven over a Tailscale HTTPS tunnel against real OpenMausBot 0.1.56, with an owner-scope and a client-scope session, the binding gap that the run exposed, and its fix.

coverage.path: openmausbot serve --tailscale -> tailscale serve https://wsh.taila20f43.ts.net -> the driver with --remote --url and a bearer token from the 0600 token file
tested: openmausbot serve --tailscale publishes the loopback server on the tailnet with an HTTPS certificate
a proxied request without a token is refused with 403 even though the server trusts loopback
openmausbot pair mints a single-use code and the driver's pair verb exchanges it into a 0600 token file
an owner-scope (admin,client) and a client-scope session, side by side, in two token files
a used pairing code replayed from the tailnet is refused in the server's own words
doctor --remote and doctor --server --remote through the tunnel with and without a token
client scope refused on an admin route (GET /api/instances)
send --remote and the lead's reply read back with status --tail --remote
a run opened locally, then watched and interrupted through the tunnel by both sessions
interrupt --remote from a client-scope session (a client-allowed route)
report, reconcile, session revocation and a clean shutdown of the tunnelled server
notTested: a second machine: the driver ran on the server's own host and reached it through the tailnet address
Telegram, OpenClaw or any other host driving the remote verbs (this run used the operator's shell)
answer --remote and an approval card through the tunnel
openmausbot --tunnel (the Tailscale Funnel/tunnel variant) or any transport other than tailscale serve
a remote watch that observes a delegation chain: only the lead ran, for one turn
token file contention between two launchers writing the same origin
a session that expires rather than being revoked
